text: Manawydan was a Welsh god, cognate with the Irish sea god Manannán mac Lir. In Wales he was associated with famine more than with sailing. He stayed linked to the Otherworld, which the Welsh placed below ground rather than out to sea. Manawydan appears in several branches of the Mabinogion. In the second branch he went to Ireland with his brother Brân the Blessed to free their sister Branwen from an abusive marriage to king Matholwch. Manawydan brought the miraculous head of his brother back to Wales. Branwen died of sorrow at the bloodshed after her safe return. Manawydan became the second husband of the queen Rhiannon in a double wedding with her son Pryderi and his beloved Cigfa. The land grew strangely barren and its people vanished into an Otherworldly mist. Manawydan proved so talented a shoemaker that rival craftsmen drove the group away. Rhiannon and Pryderi fell under an enchantment and disappeared. Farming on his own, Manawydan caught mice eating his grain and planned to execute them. The travelers who bargained for their lives revealed the mice were the disguised friends of an old enemy. By trading the rodents for his family's freedom, Manawydan reunited the two couples to a happy life.
objective: Document Manawydan, the Welsh god of the Otherworld in the Mabinogion.
